(7 goals) |prevseason= [[2018–19 Copa del Rey|2018–19]] |nextseason= [[2020–21 Copa del Rey|2020–21]] }} The '''2019–20 Copa del Rey''' was the 118th staging of the [[Copa del Rey]] (including two seasons where two rival editions were played). In its original format, the winners were assured a place in the [[2020–21 UEFA Europa League#Group stage|2020–21 UEFA Europa League group stage]], however this place was forfeited under the extraordinary circumstances of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]], with the two finalists ([[Athletic Bilbao]] and [[Real Sociedad]]) opting instead to delay the date of the postponed match. Both finalists qualified for the four-team [[2021 Supercopa de España]]. The defending champions [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] were eliminated by [[Granada CF|Granada]] in the quarter-finals. Real Sociedad won the [[2020 Copa del Rey final|final]] 1–0 against [[Basque derby|Basque rivals]] [[Athletic Bilbao]], achieving their second Copa del Rey title{{cite web |url=https://rfef.es/en/noticias/track-record-the-team-in-white-win-their-20th-copa-trophy |title=TRACK RECORD - The team in white win their 20th Copa trophy. - LIST OF WINNERS OF THE SPANISH CHAMPIONSHIP - COPA DE SM EL REY |website=RFEF.es (RFEF official website) |date=7 May 2023 |access-date=10 May 2023 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230507224626/https://rfef.es/en/noticias/track-record-the-team-in-white-win-their-20th-copa-trophy |archive-date=7 May 2023 }}{{Cite web|url=http://www.rfef.es/FCKeditor/UserFiles/File/conferencia/REVISTA%20RFEF%20141%20OK.pdf#70|title=Historial|access-date=10 May 2023|author=Real Federación Española de Fútbol|date=March 2011|magazine=Revista Oficial de la R.F.E.F.|page=70|format=pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120718164817/http://www.rfef.es/FCKeditor/UserFiles/File/conferencia/REVISTA%20RFEF%20141%20OK.pdf|archive-date=18 July 2012|url-status=dead}} (in [[1909 Copa del Rey|1909]] it was won by its forerunner, [[Club Ciclista de San Sebastián]]), ending a 34-year trophy drought since [[1987 Copa del Rey final|1987]].{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/56627359|title=Oyarzabal scores winner in Copa del Rey final|website=BBC Sport|date=3 April 2021|access-date=3 April 2021}}{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/apr/03/athletic-bilbao-real-sociedad-copa-del-rey-2020-final-match-report|title=Real Sociedad beat Athletic to claim Copa del Rey and Basque glory|first=Sid|last=Lowe|work=The Guardian|date=3 April 2021|access-date=3 April 2021}} As across Spain, match times up to 26 October 2019 and from 29 March 2020 were [[Central European Summer Time|CEST]] ([[UTC+02:00|UTC+2]]). Times on interim ("winter") days were [[Central European Time|CET]] ([[UTC+01:00|UTC+1]]). ==Schedule and format== On 29 April 2019, the assembly of the [[Royal Spanish Football Federation]] approved the new competition format,{{cite web|url=https://www.rfef.es/noticias/nueva-copa-del-rey-saldra-116-equipos|website=rfef.es|publisher=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation]]|date=29 April 2019|access-date=15 May 2019|language=es|title=La nueva Copa del Rey saldrá con 116 equipos|archive-date=9 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190509110001/https://www.rfef.es/noticias/nueva-copa-del-rey-saldra-116-equipos|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url= https://www.marca.com/futbol/copa-rey/2019/04/29/5cc6ded2468aebde488b459c.html|website=marca.com|publisher=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|date=29 April 2019|access-date=15 May 2019|language=es|title=Así quedan el calendario, y los nuevos formatos de Copa y Supercopa de la RFEF}} expanding the competition to 125 teams and changing all rounds to a single-match format until the semi-finals. [[David Arenas Torres|David Torres]] {{goal|27||63}} |goals2= |stadium= Poliesportiu Municipal |location= [[Sant Joan d'Alacant]] |attendance= 2,000 |referee= Ibáñez Juárez }} ==First round== The first round was played by all the qualified teams, except the four participants in the [[2020 Supercopa de España]], paired by a draw where the ten winners from the previous preliminary round were paired with ten teams from the [[2019–20 La Liga|La Liga]]. The remaining six teams and the 22 teams of [[2019–20 Segunda División|Segunda]] were paired with the four [[2019 Copa Federación de España|Copa Federación]] semifinalists, the 21 that compete in [[2019–20 Tercera División|Tercera]] and three from [[2019–20 Segunda División B|Segunda B]].
